Balaviswanathan @ ... vs The State Of Jharkhand & Others ... ... on 3 October, 2018 Author: Rongon Mukhopadhyay Bench: Rongon Mukhopadhyay In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi Cr. M. P. No. 1810 of 2008 --- C.R. Balaviswanathan @ Balavishwanathan C.R. .... Petitioner Versus The State of Jharkhand & others ... Opposite Parties --- Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rongon Mukhopadhyay --- For the Petitioner : Mr. Rohitabh Das, Advocate For the State : Mr. Shekhar Sinha, App --- Order No. 08 Dated 03rd October, 2018 Heard Mr. Rohitabh Das, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Shekhar Sinha, learned App for the State.
texts.facts: In this application the petitioner has prayed for quashing of the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Case No. C IV 03/2007 including the order dated 03.07.2007 passed by learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi by which cognizance has been taken for the offences punishable u/s 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner at the outset submits that the case of one of the co-accused has already been [LEAKAGE_MASK] in Cr.M.P. No. 1371 of 2010. It has further been submitted that there has been sufficient compliance of Rule 32 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and on such score the case of the other co-accused person has been [LEAKAGE_MASK] by this Court. Learned APP appearing for the State has opposed the prayer made by the petitioner. It appears that the petitioner was the then Branch Manager, I.T.C. Limited who has been prosecuted for commission of the offence u/s 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. The allegation which has been levelled in the prosecution case is that a sample of Ashirvad chilli powder C.R. Balaviswanathan @ ... vs The State Of Jharkhand & Others ... ... on 3 October, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165481801/ 1 was not labeled in accordance with the requirements of Rule 32(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules i.e. best before use is written in small letters and as per rule, the month and year should be mentioned in capital letters and hence it was misbranded which invites prosecution u/s 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. After the prosecution report was submitted, cognizance was taken by the learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi vide order dated 03.07.2007, which is under challenge in the present application. In the case of Jalaj Kumar Chatterjee in Cr.M.P. No. 1374 of 2010 the order dated 06.02.2013 was passed by this Court, the relevant portion of which reads as follows:- "Misbranded has been defined in Section 2(ix) of the Act, which reads as follows:- (ix) "misbranded"- an article of food shall be deemed to be misbranded (k) if it is not labeled in accordance with the requirements of this Act or rules made thereunder.
